questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

All in all, he had the **__more splendid__** collection of antique paintings ever.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. most splendid .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**the more splendid**" in the sentence is grammatically incorrect when comparing a singular collection to others.
 
• When referring to the highest degree of a quality (superlative), the correct form should be "**the most splendid**" rather than "more splendid."
 
• In this case, the sentence is describing the finest collection of antique paintings, which requires the superlative form.

Correct sentence: *All in all, he had the most splendid collection of antique paintings ever*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degrees:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Use "more" or add "-er" to adjectives when comparing two things.
 
• **Example:** This painting is **more splendid** than the other.
 
• **Usage:** Used when comparing two items or entities.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degrees:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Use "most" or add "-est" to adjectives when comparing three or more things.
 
• **Example:** This is the **most splendid** painting in the gallery.
 
• **Usage:** Used when referring to the highest degree of a quality among three or more items.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The company plans to **__expand__** its operations into global markets soon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Restrict**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Expand"** means to increase in size, scope, or extent; to make something larger or more extensive. (विस्तार करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The company decided to expand its product line to cater to a larger audience.
 
 
 
• **"Restrict"** means to limit or control the size, scope, or extent of something; to prevent it from becoming larger or spreading. (सीमित करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The government implemented new laws to restrict the use of plastic bags.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Expand'** is **'Restrict'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Restrict**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Eliminate** (नष्ट करना): To remove or get rid of something completely.

 
 
• **Example:** The new policy aims to eliminate corruption from the system.
 
 
 
• **Spread** (फैलाना): To distribute over a larger area or to make something extend broadly.
 
 
• **Example:** The news spread quickly across the town.
 
 
 
• **Diversify** (विविधता लाना): To add variety or expand into different areas.
 
 
• **Example:** The company decided to diversify its investments to reduce risks.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My brother trains young girls at the football academy, whereas I gets a handsome salary to teach mathematics at the same place.

options.text: to teach mathematics at the same place

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. I gets a handsome salary .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the verb **"gets"** in the segment **"I gets a handsome salary"**.
 
• The subject **"I"** requires the base form of the verb, which is **"get"** instead of **"gets."**
 
• Correct usage: "I get a handsome salary" because the subject "I" takes the base verb form in the present tense.

Correct sentence: *My brother trains young girls at the football academy, whereas I **get** a handsome salary to teach mathematics at the same place*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• In English grammar, the verb must agree with the subject in number and person.
 
• For singular first-person pronouns like "I," the base form of the verb is used (e.g., "I get," "I teach").
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using third-person singular verb forms (e.g., "gets") with first-person singular pronouns (e.g., "I") is incorrect.
 
• Such errors can lead to grammatical inconsistencies and should be avoided.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The bread was __**drier **__and stale.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. dry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses "drier and stale," which is incorrect because "drier" is already a comparative form.
 
• The correct option is "dry," as it simplifies the sentence and avoids redundancy.
 
• "Much drier" (option 2) is also grammatically correct but changes the meaning slightly by adding emphasis, which is unnecessary here.
 
• Option 3 ("driest") and option 4 ("more drier") are incorrect. "Driest" is a superlative form and doesn't fit the context, while "more drier" is grammatically incorrect as double comparatives shouldn't be used.

Correct sentence: *The bread was dry and stale.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Forms:**
 
 
• Comparatives like "drier" are used to compare two things.
 
• Superlatives like "driest" are used to describe the highest degree among three or more things.
 
 
 
• **Grammar Rule:** Avoid redundancy in comparative forms (e.g., "more drier").
</ul

questions.question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Johannes Gutenberg invented the first printing press that could print thousands of __________ a day. This made books cheaper and information __________ widely available.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Johannes Gutenberg invented the first printing press that revolutionized the dissemination of knowledge.
 
• The word "**pages**" fits the context appropriately, as books are made of pages.
 
• The word "**more**" correctly signifies the increased availability of information.
 
• The other options: "**sheet; much**," "**leaf; many**," and "**sides; most**" do not fit the context as accurately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Johannes Gutenberg invented the first printing press that could print thousands of pages__ a day. This made books cheaper and information __more__ widely available.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Sheet**: Refers to a single piece of paper, but doesn’t fit the pluralized context of printed material.
 
• **Leaf**: Refers to a single page of a book, but isn’t commonly used in this context.
 
• **Sides**: Refers to the two faces of a piece of paper, but doesn’t align with the meaning of pages.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Although she is usually / rude with everyone, / she behaved nice / with all of us today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. she behaved nice .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word **"nice"** is incorrectly used as it is an adjective. The correct form is to use an adverb **"nicely"** to describe the verb *behaved*.
 
• An adverb is required to modify a verb, and the word *behaved* is a verb in this sentence.
 
• The corrected segment should be: **"she behaved nicely"**.

Correct sentence: *Although she is usually rude with everyone, she behaved **nicely** with all of us today*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjectives vs. Adverbs:**
 
 
• **Adjectives:** Describe nouns or pronouns (e.g., nice, beautiful).
 
• **Adverbs:** Describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs (e.g., nicely, beautifully).
 
• **Rule:** When describing how an action is performed, use an adverb.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options

options.text: An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team.
An unexpected power failure completely foiled a plan of a team.
A unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of a team.
An unexpected power failure completely foiled an plan of the team.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct sentence needs to follow proper grammar rules, including the use of articles and subject-verb agreement.
 
• Option 1 is correct because:
 
 
• **"An"** is the correct article to use before a word starting with a vowel sound like "unexpected."
 
• The phrase **"the plan of the team"** correctly specifies the particular plan of the specific team, making the sentence grammatically accurate.
 
 
 
• Other options are incorrect due to the following errors:
 
 
• **Option 2:** "a plan of a team" is too generic and lacks specificity, which makes it less precise in the context.
 
• **Option 3:** "A unexpected" is incorrect because "A" cannot be used before a word starting with a vowel sound; "An" should be used instead.
 
• **Option 4:** "An plan" is incorrect because "An" cannot be used before a word starting with a consonant sound; it should be "A plan."
 
 

Correct sentence: *An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Articles:**
 
 
• **"A"** is used before words starting with a consonant sound (e.g., "a team").
 
• **"An"** is used before words starting with a vowel sound (e.g., "an unexpected event").
 
• **"The"** is used to refer to something specific or already mentioned (e.g., "the plan of the team").
 
 
 
• Carefully choosing articles ensures the grammatical accuracy of the sentence.
</ul
